question_text: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after falling off a staircase and hitting his head on the handrail. He was unconscious for 10 minutes and vomited twice. On arrival, he is drowsy. Examination shows a fixed, dilated left pupil and right-sided flaccid paralysis. A CT scan of the head shows a skull fracture in the region of the pterion and a biconvex hyperdensity overlying the left frontotemporal lobe. This patient's condition is most likely caused by damage to a vessel that enters the skull through which of the following foramina?
